newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares fall on profit-taking, caution.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares fall on profit-taking, caution.

text.p: Istanbul shares fell in expected profit-taking on Friday after Thursday's 5.43 percent surge, but recovered from early lows on mild support, brokers said.
They said caution also increased due to political uncertainty mounting ahead of a censure motion debate awaited in parliament next week to topple the Islamist-conservative coaliton government.

The IMKB National-100 closed 23 points, or 1.52 percent lower at 1,492, but up from a day's low of 1,479. Trade volume shrank to 17.67 trillion lira ($128.4 million) from Thursday's 24.47 trillion ($178.7 million).

"There is support at the index's 1,480 level which helped to trigger a mild recovery today. But sales continued because the market is still indexed to politics," said Huseyin Istanbullu from Meksa securities.
Four opposition parties submitted a censure motion to topple Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's coalition.
The index soared 8.6 percent in the past three days on the rising prospect of a new secularist pact to exclude the ruling Islamists.

Erez, a former minister of the conservative True Path Party (DYP) has been the chief coordinator of the recent move to unseat the government. But the DYP started a disciplionary move against Erez which could result in his sacking from the party.

The motion requires an absolute majority of 276 votes, so it will need the support of government MPs to bring down the coalition. Erez and conservative opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz have said there was support from within the DYP.
